declarations.docstring: Auxiliary predicate on partitions of a natural number.
Under the auxiliary restriction of a complex permutation representation, the degree-m comparison element acts as the degree-(m+1) auxiliary element.
The auxiliary partition predicate holds exactly when the integer-valued statistic is constant on all associated degree-m partitions.
Rotation on `Fin (m + 1)` sends the cast of `k : Fin m` to its successor.
The monoid homomorphism lifting permutations of `Fin m` to permutations of `Fin (m + 1)` while fixing zero.
The zero-fixing permutation lift is the conjugate of the last-fixing lift by rotation.
The zero-fixing lift sends the successor of an index to the successor of its image.
The zero-fixing lift of a transposition is the transposition of the corresponding successor indices.
Every zero-fixing permutation lift sends zero to zero.
The last-fixing lift sends a cast index to the cast of its image.
Every last-fixing permutation lift fixes the last index.
The auxiliary restricted partition coefficient is one on associated partitions and zero otherwise.
Auxiliary construction restricting a complex representation of permutations of `Fin (m + 1)` to permutations of `Fin m`.
A partition evaluation has the same value on the zero-fixing and last-fixing lifts of a permutation.
Evaluating a partition at a zero-fixing lift equals the sum of the lower-degree evaluations over its associated partitions.
In the auxiliary partition representation, applying an algebra element to a supported vector agrees with multiplication by that element.
An auxiliary element of the degree-n algebra, available when n is nonzero.
The auxiliary degree-(m+1) element acts by one scalar on the partition-supported subspace exactly when the partition statistic is constant on all associated degree-m partitions.
For a fixed complex scalar, scalar action by the auxiliary degree-(m+1) element on the partition-supported subspace is equivalent to equality of every associated partition statistic with that scalar.
A second auxiliary element of the degree-n algebra, available when n is nonzero.
The secondary auxiliary degree element has a scalar action on the partition-supported subspace exactly when the auxiliary partition predicate holds.
In a finite-dimensional complex permutation representation, the secondary auxiliary degree element has an eigenbasis, and each eigenvalue is an integer between `1 - n` and `n - 1`.
The secondary auxiliary degree element is the difference of the comparison element and the auxiliary degree element.
Every eigenvalue of the secondary auxiliary element in a finite-dimensional complex degree-(m+1) permutation representation is an integer.
For a partition with r copies of c, the secondary auxiliary degree element acts on every supported vector by the scalar `c - r`.
